明.west: Like Apollo, the bringer of light — clarity that dispels doubt.
明.note: Reads open and lucid. Avoid pairing with another light character.
明.lineEn: The Book of Songs: shining below, resplendent above.

光.west: The Promethean spark — light carried from the gods to ordinary hands.
光.note: Strong and short. Works well as a second character, rarely as a first.
光.lineEn: The Book of Changes: inner brilliance waits for the right season to shine.

曜.m: sunlight; the shining of the sun and stars
曜.west: Helios driving his chariot — the daily return of light.
曜.note: Rare and literary. Best for readers who want something uncommon.
曜.lineEn: The Book of Songs: the fur robe gleams like the sun at daybreak.

曦.m: the light of the rising sun
曦.west: Eos, the rosy-fingered dawn of Homer — beginning, not ending.
曦.note: Very soft and feminine. Strokes are heavy; pair with a simpler character.
曦.lineEn: Songs of Chu: the sun sinks west, its light still turning back.

晨.west: Aurora opening the gates for the sun — the quiet hour before everything starts.
晨.note: Warm and unpretentious. Common in modern names without feeling generic.
晨.lineEn: The Book of Songs: how goes the night? The night draws toward dawn.

昕.m: dawn, the first light of day
昕.west: The first crack of light in Genesis — order spoken into darkness.
昕.note: Rare but easy to read. Good when the surname is already complex.
昕.lineEn: The Book of Songs: the red bow loosened, joy at the guest who arrives at first light.

灿.west: A shield of polished bronze catching the sun — splendor that protects.
灿.note: Bright and modern. Reads well with single-syllable surnames.
灿.lineEn: Yueyang Tower: morning glow and evening shade, a thousand moods.

德.west: Arete — excellence of character that others orient themselves by.
德.note: Very traditional. Still strong, but pair with a lighter character to stay modern.
德.lineEn: The Analects: rule by virtue, and you are the pole star the others turn around.

仁.west: Caritas — the goodwill that holds a community together.
仁.note: Only four strokes, so it balances long surnames beautifully.
仁.lineEn: The Analects: asked about ren, the Master said — love people.

礼.west: Civitas — the courteous forms that let strangers live together.
礼.note: Dignified. Slightly formal, so it suits adult names rather than childhood ones.
礼.lineEn: The Analects: to restrain oneself and return to ritual — that is ren.

信.west: Fides — the Roman goddess of good faith, older than any contract.
信.note: Blunt and honest. Best as a second character after a softer first one.
信.lineEn: The Analects: in dealings with friends, have I been unfaithful?

诚.west: Knightly troth — the word given that is never taken back.
诚.note: Warm and direct. Pairs well with water or wood characters.
诚.lineEn: The Book of Rites: sincerity is the way of heaven; to be sincere is the way of people.

善.west: The Good beyond being in Plato — what everything aims at without saying so.
善.note: Gentle and generous. Slightly feminine-leaning in modern usage.
善.lineEn: Tao Te Ching: the highest good is like water, which benefits all things and does not contend.

谦.west: Socratic ignorance — wisdom that begins by admitting how little it knows.
谦.note: Understated. Excellent for a quiet, confident impression.
谦.lineEn: The Book of Changes: humility succeeds; the noble one carries things through.

毅.west: Perseverance of the Stoics — the will that outlasts circumstance.
毅.note: Firm and masculine. Avoid clustering with other harsh-sounding characters.
毅.lineEn: The Analects: a scholar must be broad-minded and resolute — the burden is heavy, the road long.

恒.west: The fixed purpose of Odysseus — the mast bound, the course held.
恒.note: Plain and dependable. Never sounds dated.
恒.lineEn: The Analects: a person without constancy in virtue will sooner or later be shamed.

正.west: Rectitude in the old Roman sense — a line drawn straight.
正.note: Very short and crisp. Strong with two-syllable surnames.
正.lineEn: The Analects: when the leader is himself upright, the work proceeds without orders.

温.west: The tempered heat of a well-made sword — warmth with an edge.
温.note: Soft and approachable. Suits both genders, leans feminine in modern usage.
温.lineEn: The Analects: the Master was mild yet firm, dignified yet not fierce.

雅.west: Grace in the Renaissance sense — proportion that needs no ornament.
雅.note: Polished and slightly literary. Good for a name meant to sound composed.
雅.lineEn: The Book of Songs: the ya are the orthodox odes, where the rise and fall of good rule is told.

文.west: Humanitas — letters that make a person more fully human.
文.note: Only four strokes. One of the safest, most versatile naming characters.
文.lineEn: The Analects: when substance and refinement are in balance, there is a noble person.

思.west: Mnemosyne, mother of the muses — memory and thought before speech.
思.note: Gentle and introspective. Reads feminine today but has always been neutral.
思.lineEn: The Book of Songs: blue, blue the collar — my heart goes on and on.

书.west: The library at Alexandria — knowledge that outlives the hand that wrote it.
书.note: Clean and quiet. Very good as a middle character.
书.lineEn: Records of the Grand Historian: to probe heaven and humanity, and speak in one voice of my own.

学.west: The scholar’s lamp — study as a lifelong practice rather than a stage.
学.note: Direct and unpretentious. Slightly earnest, which many families want.
学.lineEn: The Analects: to learn and rehearse it in season — is that not a joy?

哲.west: Philosophia — the love of wisdom, not its possession.
哲.note: Sturdy and masculine. Common enough to be comfortable, rare enough to be distinct.
哲.lineEn: The Book of Documents: deep wisdom and cultured brightness, mild courtesy truly filled.

睿.west: Prudentia, the Roman virtue that sees what is coming.
睿.note: Strong and slightly formal. Works well with a soft first character.
睿.lineEn: The Book of Documents: reflection is called astuteness; astuteness becomes sageliness.

博.west: Encyclopedic curiosity — the Renaissance ideal of knowing widely.
博.note: Generous and open. Reads confident rather than intellectual.
博.lineEn: The Analects: broaden me with culture, restrain me with ritual.

渊.west: The deep well behind the house — quiet supply that never runs dry.
渊.note: Quiet and serious. Pairs naturally with water characters.
渊.lineEn: Tao Te Ching: deep, like the ancestor of all things.

涵.m: to contain; depth of character; tolerance
涵.west: The harbor that holds every ship — capacity rather than display.
涵.note: Very popular in recent decades; comfortable and gently feminine.
涵.lineEn: History of Song: of deep cultivation, with principle when events press.

聪.west: Sharp-eared Telemachus — attention as the root of understanding.
聪.note: Cheerful. Slightly childlike, so consider whether you want it in an adult name.
聪.lineEn: The Book of Documents: to hear well is called intelligence.

敏.west: Alacrity — the readiness that makes discipline look easy.
敏.note: Light and efficient. Traditionally used for both genders.
敏.lineEn: The Analects: quick in action, careful in speech.

颖.m: the tip of an ear of grain; outstanding talent
颖.west: The blade that shows through the sheath — talent that cannot stay hidden.
颖.note: Bright and modern. Often paired with 涵 or 慧.
颖.lineEn: Records of the Grand Historian: had the awl been in the bag sooner, its point would have shown through.

志.west: The archer’s aim — purpose that selects one target and ignores the rest.
志.note: Firm and classic. One of the most durable masculine characters.
志.lineEn: The Book of Documents: poetry speaks the purpose; song draws it out.

远.west: Horizon-seeking — the Greek nostos that never settles for the near shore.
远.note: Spacious. Works best as a second character.
远.lineEn: The Analects: the burden is heavy and the road is far.

宏.west: The vault of a Roman basilica — a scale that lifts the head.
宏.note: Broad and confident. Slightly formal in tone.
宏.lineEn: The Book of Documents: vast as heaven.

鹏.m: the roc, a legendary bird of immense span
鹏.west: The eagle of Zeus — the flight that sees the whole field at once.
鹏.note: Bold and aspirational. Very masculine in modern usage.
鹏.lineEn: Zhuangzi: the back of the Peng — no one knows how many thousand li it spans.

鸿.west: The migrating goose that keeps its V through weather — loyalty plus reach.
鸿.note: Poised and literary. Also carries the sense of a letter from far away.
鸿.lineEn: Records of the Grand Historian: how should a sparrow know the ambition of the swan?

骏.west: Bucephalus — the horse only one rider could mount.
骏.note: Energetic and masculine. Pair with a calmer first character.
骏.lineEn: The Book of Songs: four stallions strong, we drive east.

帆.west: The sail unfurled — departure taken as a promise.
帆.note: Light and optimistic. Modern but not trendy.
帆.lineEn: Li Bai: a time will come to ride the long wind and break the waves.

峰.west: The summit that is earned by the climb, not granted by the map.
峰.note: Solid and masculine. Very common, so consider pairing freshly.
峰.lineEn: Ouyang Xiu: the peak turns, the path bends, and a pavilion spreads its wings above the spring.

岳.west: Mount Olympus — the height where the air is thin and clear.
岳.note: Weighty and dignified. Good after a single-syllable surname.
岳.lineEn: The Book of Songs: the tall sacred peak rises to heaven.

山.west: The unmoved mountain of the Psalms — refuge that does not shift.
山.note: Only three strokes. Striking and minimal in a two-character name.
山.lineEn: The Analects: the wise delight in water, the good delight in mountains.

川.west: Heraclitus’ river — the same and never the same.
川.note: Flowing and open. Balances a heavy surname well.
川.lineEn: The Analects: standing by the river, the Master said — it goes on like this, day and night.

海.west: The mare oceanum — the boundary the Romans feared and crossed anyway.
海.note: Vast and generous. Very common, so the second character must do more work.
海.lineEn: Zhuangzi: of all waters under heaven, none is greater than the sea.

澜.west: The wave that carries rather than drowns, if you read the water right.
澜.note: Slightly dramatic and elegant. Good for a second character.
澜.lineEn: Mencius: there is an art to watching water — watch where it breaks into waves.

云.west: The cloud that takes any shape — freedom without formlessness.
云.note: Light and airy. Extremely popular, which cuts both ways.
云.lineEn: Yueyang Tower: the bright moon for a thousand li, light leaping on the water.

月.west: Selene — the light that makes the dark navigable.
月.note: Quiet and classic. Almost always feminine in modern names.
月.lineEn: The Book of Songs: the moon comes out, bright; the lovely one is fair.

星.west: The lodestar — a fixed point used to find the way home.
星.note: Bright and friendly. Neutral in gender.
星.lineEn: The Book of Songs: those little stars, three and five in the east.

辰.m: celestial body; the hour; the dragon sign
辰.west: Kairos — the right moment, seized rather than waited for.
辰.note: Strong and slightly archaic in a good way. One of the twelve zodiac branches.
辰.lineEn: The Book of Songs: heaven gave me life — where do my hours fall?

松.west: The evergreen of the northern myths — life that refuses the season.
松.note: Steady and masculine. Slightly old-fashioned, which some families prefer.
松.lineEn: The Analects: only in the cold of the year do we learn the pine outlasts.

竹.west: The reed of Aesop that bends and survives the storm.
竹.note: Clean and upright. A quiet, principled impression.
竹.lineEn: Ode to Bamboo: joints before it breaks ground, still hollow at the height of clouds.

梅.west: The winter flower of the Persephone myth — beauty timed against the cold.
梅.note: Classically feminine and dignified. Very readable for foreigners.
梅.lineEn: Lin Bu: sparse shadows slant across the shallow water; hidden fragrance drifts at dusk.

兰.west: The hidden violet of the Odyssey — nobility that grows away from applause.
兰.note: Refined and gentle. One of the most durable feminine characters.
兰.lineEn: Songs of Chu: I planted nine acres of orchids and a hundred of basil.

荷.west: The lotus of Egyptian cosmology — creation rising from the silt.
荷.note: Soft and clean. Best for feminine names; reads a little uncommon in English eyes.
荷.lineEn: On the Love of the Lotus: out of mud without stain, rinsed by clear water without coquetry.

林.west: The sacred grove of the Druids — many trunks, one canopy.
林.note: Easy to pronounce and remember. Neutral gender.
林.lineEn: The Book of Songs: the crane stands in the forest, apart from the flock.

静.west: Hesychia — the stillness of the desert fathers, where noise ends.
静.note: Very common in feminine names. Pair with a character that has movement.
静.lineEn: Tao Te Ching: reach the extreme of emptiness, hold fast to stillness.

淑.west: The noble lady of courtly love — worth that is cultivated, not announced.
淑.note: Traditional and feminine. Reads slightly old-fashioned but with dignity.
淑.lineEn: The Book of Songs: the modest and good woman — a mate for the noble man.

婉.west: The gentle curve of a well-made bow — strength that does not announce itself.
婉.note: Soft and slightly sweet. Beautiful with wood or water characters.
婉.lineEn: The Book of Songs: there is a lovely one — clear-browed and graceful.

宁.west: Pax — peace as a condition actively kept, not merely the absence of war.
宁.note: Short and calm. Neutral but frequently feminine in modern use.
宁.lineEn: The Book of Songs: when the troubles are settled, there is both safety and peace.

和.west: Harmonia — the tuning that makes separate strings sound like one chord.
和.note: Warm and balanced. Works for both genders.
和.lineEn: The Analects: in the use of ritual, harmony is what matters.

泰.west: The golden age of Saturn — a season when things hold their place.
泰.lineEn: The Book of Changes: Tai — the small departs, the great arrives; auspicious.

安.west: The hearth — the small circle of warmth that makes the world manageable.
安.note: Very short and friendly. One of the easiest names for foreigners to say.
安.lineEn: Tao Te Ching: let them be settled in their homes and glad in their customs.

琳.west: The gem of the lapidary — beauty made by patience and pressure.
琳.note: Elegant and feminine. Very readable in English contexts.
琳.lineEn: The Book of Songs: the jade pendants ring against one another as he walks.

瑾.m: fine jade; also meaning virtue concealed
瑾.west: The buried treasure of the old tales — value that does not need an audience.
瑾.note: Literary and slightly rare. Strong for either gender.
瑾.lineEn: Songs of Chu: I hold jade in my bosom and in my hand, and know not to whom to show it.

瑜.west: The pearl of great price — worth that justifies the whole search.
瑜.note: Smooth and feminine. Pairs well with 瑾 for twins.
瑜.lineEn: Songs of Chu: jade held in the bosom, jade held in the hand.

璇.m: beautiful jade; the second star of the Dipper
璇.west: Polaris — the star that holds still while everything else turns.
璇.note: Striking and feminine. A little rare, which suits distinctive names.
璇.lineEn: The Book of Documents: the jade sighting tube aligned to set the seven governors in order.

琪.west: The reciprocal gift — generosity that expects nothing but returns everything.
琪.note: Friendly and warm. Common in feminine names without being plain.
琪.lineEn: The Book of Songs: you gave me a peach; I return a jewel.

瑞.west: The favourable omen of the augurs — a sign read before the journey starts.
瑞.note: Neutral and optimistic. Very common, so pair thoughtfully.
瑞.lineEn: Wang Chong: a rui is the sign of a blessing on its way.

瑶.west: The crystal of the fairy tales — clarity that shows only what is there.
瑶.note: Soft and feminine. A gentle, slightly dreamy name.
瑶.lineEn: The Book of Songs: you gave me a peach; I return a jewel.

清.west: The spring of living water — purity that refreshes rather than excludes.
清.note: Extremely versatile. Works in almost any name.
清.lineEn: Songs of Chu: when the Canglang water is clear, I may wash my cap-string.

澄.west: Still water in the sun — depth you can see straight through.
澄.note: Slightly uncommon. Gives a name a quiet sophistication.
澄.lineEn: A New Account of the Tales of the World: clarify it and it is not clearer; muddy it and it is not clouded.

朗.west: The clear sky after a storm — relief you can feel.
朗.note: Open and masculine. Reads friendly rather than hard.
朗.lineEn: The Book of Jin: of clear bone and fine bearing, his presence bright and open.

润.west: The oil of anointing — what makes hard things move.
润.note: Smooth and understated. Balanced gender lean.
润.lineEn: The Book of Changes: wind and rain enrich the world.

熙.west: The harvest festival of the old calendar — abundance shared, not hoarded.
熙.note: Warm and auspicious. On the rise in recent years.
熙.lineEn: The Book of Songs: the royal army raised, its time of brightness came.

景.west: The prospect from the watchtower — the view earned by climbing.
景.note: Confident and slightly formal. Very masculine.
景.lineEn: Yueyang Tower: when spring is mild and the light is bright, the waves lie still.

嘉.west: The guest-friend of Homeric hospitality — arrival itself as a good thing.
嘉.note: Warm and generous. Excellent first character.
嘉.lineEn: The Book of Songs: I have a fine guest — come, play the strings and pipes.

福.west: Beatitudo — fortune that includes the ending, not just the peak.
福.note: Very direct. Traditional and unambiguous; may read old-fashioned.
福.lineEn: The Book of Documents: the five blessings — long life, wealth, health, virtue, and a good end.

荣.west: The laurel crown — honour that is worn, then grows back.
荣.note: Masculine-leaning. Strong and positive with a slightly competitive edge.
荣.lineEn: Songs of Chu: green leaves and white blossoms, abundant and lovely.

翔.m: to soar, to circle in flight
翔.west: Daedalus’s flight — the freedom that must respect its own limits.
翔.note: Free and airy. Very masculine in modern usage.
翔.lineEn: Songs of Chu: high flying, peacefully soaring, riding clear air and the two powers.

衡.west: The scales of the Roman law court — fairness made visible.
衡.lineEn: The Book of Documents: unify the pitch, the measures, the weights.

天.west: The open sky of the Stoics — order you can trust without seeing its author.
天.note: Four strokes, iconic, and every reader knows it. Strong as a first character.
天.lineEn: The Book of Songs: heaven gave birth to the people, and with them came measure and law.

宇.m: the whole space of the world; eaves
宇.west: The cosmos as a habitable room — the roof that covers everything.
宇.note: Modern and spacious. Pairs beautifully with water or light characters.
宇.lineEn: Zhuangzi: what has reality but no fixed place — that is space.

昊.west: The boundless noon — scale that makes small things honest.
昊.note: Bold and masculine. Slightly rare, which keeps it memorable.
昊.lineEn: The Book of Songs: vast is the sky, yet its virtue does not extend.

卓.west: The peak that stands clear of the ridge line — excellence visible from afar.
卓.note: Crisp and confident. Reads well with almost any surname.
卓.lineEn: The Analects: I have exhausted my ability, and there it stands, upright before me.

越.west: To cross the boundary that was supposed to hold — and be right to.
越.note: Energetic. Good as a second character to mark progress.
越.lineEn: Zhuangzi: the cook may neglect the kitchen, but the priest does not step over the wine vessels to take his place.

承.m: to carry, to receive and continue
承.west: Tradition in the best sense — the torch handed on still burning.
承.note: Warm and grounded. Says "you are trusted with something."
承.lineEn: The Book of Changes: to receive heaven and move with the season.

铭.west: The inscription cut into stone — a promise that outlasts the hand.
铭.note: Distinctive and slightly formal. Excellent for a name meant to be remembered.
铭.lineEn: The Book of Rites: on the bath basin of Tang was engraved — renew yourself daily, again and again.

钦.west: Reverence before the measured order of things — attention as a virtue.
钦.note: Formal and steady. Reads slightly classic, which suits adult names.
钦.lineEn: The Book of Documents: reverently follow the vast sky, charting sun, moon and stars.

立.west: The column that holds its own weight — independence without display.
立.note: Very short. Striking next to a two-character given name.
立.lineEn: The Analects: at thirty, I stood.

达.west: The open road rather than the wall — understanding that travels.
达.note: Friendly and unpretentious. Good with a softer first character.
达.lineEn: The Analects: Ci is penetrating — what difficulty would government be for him?

通.west: The bridge rather than the gate — connection as the higher skill.
通.note: Practical and warm. Rarely used, which makes it stand out.
通.lineEn: The Book of Changes: penetrate their changes, and the pattern of heaven and earth completes itself.

元.m: the first, the origin, the head
元.west: Genesis in miniature — the beginning that contains the whole.
元.note: Four strokes and very strong. A classic first character.
元.lineEn: The Book of Changes: the origin is the head of all that is good.

阳.m: the sunlit side; yang, the active principle
阳.west: Solar warmth as a principle, not a mood — the side of things that acts.
阳.note: Warm and open. Extremely common, so the second character should be choiceful.
阳.lineEn: The Book of Changes: one yin and one yang — that is called the Way.

永.west: The vow that is meant literally — duration as a form of loyalty.
永.note: Classic and calm. Works for either gender.
永.lineEn: The Book of Songs: not as repayment, but that we may be friends forever.

大.west: Magnanimity — greatness that has no need to be noticed.
大.note: Only three strokes. Very bold; usually paired with a dense character.
大.lineEn: Tao Te Ching: the greatest sound is scarcely heard; the greatest image has no form.

中.m: the middle; centered, hitting the mark
中.west: The golden mean of Aristotle — the point between two failures.
中.note: Simple and balanced. Reads modest, which is its charm.
中.lineEn: The Analects: the middle way as a virtue — is it not the highest?

义.west: Justice as a debt owed, not a feeling held.
义.note: Only three strokes but very weighty. Powerful with a light first character.
义.lineEn: Mencius: life is what I want, and rightness is what I want; if I cannot have both, I give up life for rightness.

敬.west: The attention that treats small things as if they mattered. Because they do.
敬.note: Dignified. Slightly formal, good for a considered name.
敬.lineEn: The Book of Songs: be reverent, be reverent — heaven sees clearly.

恭.west: The bow that is not submission but recognition.
恭.note: Quiet and polite. Rarely used today, so it reads distinctive.
恭.lineEn: The Analects: courtesy keeps insult away; generosity wins people.

惠.west: Grace as a practical gift — kindness that shows up in the ledger.
惠.note: Traditionally feminine. Warm without being soft.
惠.lineEn: The Analects: he nourished the people with kindness and employed them with fairness.

慈.west: The compassion that makes courage possible — love that does not flinch.
慈.note: Gentle and strong at once. Slightly maternal in tone.
慈.lineEn: Tao Te Ching: because of compassion, one can be brave.

康.west: Salus — wellbeing treated as a public good, not a private mood.
康.note: Friendly and optimistic. Very common but never tiresome.
康.lineEn: The Book of Documents: the third blessing is health and peace.

宝.west: The treasure in the field — value discovered rather than displayed.
宝.note: Very warm and affectionate. A name people smile at.
宝.lineEn: The Book of Rites: the state of Chu has no treasure but goodness — that is its treasure.

悦.west: Joy as a by-product of doing the right thing — not a goal in itself.
悦.note: Bright and friendly. Modern favourite, but reads sincere.
悦.lineEn: Mencius: how rightness delights my heart, as rich food delights my mouth.

欣.west: The lifting of spirits that a good meal and good company can produce.
欣.note: Open and cheerful. Works well as a first character.
欣.lineEn: The Book of Songs: the good wine brings gladness, the roasted meat gives fragrance.

怡.west: Serenity that is chosen rather than found — comfort with one’s own company.
怡.note: Soft and comfortable. Very popular in feminine names.

恬.west: Ataraxia — the untroubled calm of the Epicurean garden.
恬.note: Gentle and rare. Reads thoughtful rather than passive.
恬.lineEn: Zhuangzi: those of old who governed by the Way used stillness to nourish understanding.

慧.west: Sophia — wisdom as a person, not a quantity.
慧.note: Common in feminine names. Strong and traditional.

芸.west: The herb grown not for show but for its use — quiet usefulness.
芸.note: Very elegant and slightly literary. Popular in modern names.
芸.lineEn: The Book of Songs: to the left, the noble one fits there; to the right, the noble one holds it.

芷.m: angelica; a fragrant plant of the marshes
芷.west: The flower of the Odyssey picked before nightfall — beauty that must be gathered.
芷.note: Refined and distinctive. A little literary for everyday use, which is its appeal.
芷.lineEn: Songs of Chu: I wore wild ginger and angelica, and strung autumn orchids as pendants.

莲.west: The lotus of the Nile creation myth — order rising out of silt.
莲.note: Soft and traditional. Pairs well with water characters.
莲.lineEn: On the Love of the Lotus: from mud unstained, washed in clear water without coquetry.

薇.m: a wild vetch eaten by soldiers on campaign
薇.west: The plant that grows where the army passes — endurance recorded in something small.
薇.note: Very popular and very readable. Gentle and slightly florid.
薇.lineEn: The Book of Songs: when I went away, the willows swayed; now I return, sleet falls thick.

露.west: The transient bead of dawn — beauty that is honest about its hour.
露.note: Delicate but heavy in strokes. Needs a simple second character.
露.lineEn: The Book of Songs: in the field the creepers grow, and the dew lies round.

晴.west: The clearing sky after the storm — relief with no effort in it.
晴.note: Bright and open. Very friendly for feminine names.
晴.lineEn: Cui Hao: on the clear river the Hanyang trees stand distinct; rank grasses fill the Parrot Isle.

岩.west: The rock of the abbey — what remains when weather has had its way.
岩.note: Hard and confident. Very masculine; balances a softer second character.
岩.lineEn: The Book of Songs: the southern hills rise steep, and the stones stand sheer.

桐.west: The tree cut for music — usefulness that becomes something better than itself.
桐.note: Quiet and upright. Rare enough to feel distinct.
桐.lineEn: The Book of Songs: catalpa and paulownia, lacquer and cypress — cut to make lutes and zithers.

洛.m: the River Luo; a great river name
洛.west: A river that made a civilisation — place as destiny.
洛.note: Smooth and modern. Popular for both genders.
洛.lineEn: The Book of Songs: look at the Luo — how vast and deep the water runs.

沛.west: The storm that ends the drought — plenty arriving faster than expected.
沛.lineEn: Mencius: heaven gathers the clouds, and the rain comes down in abundance.

舟.west: Charon’s skiff turned toward the future instead — passage as a choice.
舟.note: Small and clear. Reads calm rather than adventurous.
舟.lineEn: The Book of Songs: drifting that cypress boat, drifting on the current.

溪.west: The brook that always finds the sea — persistence without particular force.
溪.note: Soft and feminine-leaning. A gentle, unforced name.
溪.lineEn: Tao Te Ching: the Way in the world is as valleys and streams to the rivers and seas.

泓.west: The deep pool whose surface is quiet — reserve rather than absence.
泓.note: Clean and uncommon. Reads capable, not showy.
泓.lineEn: The Book of Songs: how vast and deep the water — depth is what it has to offer.
